key_insight: Multilingual machine learning on connected speech can distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic PPA in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals with high accuracy, even across both languages.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more scalable aphasia subtype screening for bilingual patients when full language assessments are difficult to provide.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients (24 lvPPA, 10 nfvPPA) completed a picture-description task in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Four feature sets were extracted from speech: timing metrics, word-level parameters, linguistic features, and image-text congruence scores.
Classifiers were trained separately and then combined into an ensemble model; performance was compared between languages with McNemar testing.
evidence_signal: The strongest models reached macro-F1 scores of 93% for word-level features in the non-dominant language and 92% for the ensemble in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference by language.
watch_item: Results come from a small single-cohort sample, so broader validation and real-world workflow testing are needed before implementation.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
